summary_html: Federal transparency statutes—**FOIA** and **Sunshine Act**—require disclosure of government data. Project Milk Carton promotes FOIA requests and public dashboards for child-welfare records.
authority_html:
- **Freedom of Information Act (5 U.S.C. § 552)** — public access to records  
- **Government in the Sunshine Act (5 U.S.C. § 552b)** — open-meeting requirements

key_cases.case_name: In re Records of the Department of Children & Family Services (Sarasota Herald-Tribune v. Department of Children & Family Services)
key_cases.court: District Court of Appeal of Florida, Second District
key_cases.holding: A circuit court considering a petition for access to confidential child abuse records must conduct an in camera review before ruling; refusing to inspect the records was an abuse of discretion and the denial of access was reversed.
key_cases.relevance: This is the operative Florida authority for public-records access to child welfare files.
key_cases.quote: the circuit court abused its discretion when it failed to conduct an in camera review of the records to which the Herald-Tribune seeks access

key_cases.case_name: Department of Health & Rehabilitative Services v. Gainesville Sun Publishing Co.
key_cases.court: District Court of Appeal of Florida, First District
key_cases.holding: A trial court may order confidential child abuse records produced for in camera inspection and may find good cause for disclosure without an evidentiary hearing, balancing the child's and siblings' privacy against the public interest in evaluating agency performance.
key_cases.relevance: It is the earliest Florida appellate authority letting the press obtain confidential abuse records on a good-cause showing.
key_cases.quote: Under the circumstances of this case, the trial court did not err in finding good cause for disclosure without an evidentiary hearing.
